text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "config/regions.yaml defines three regions: NVL (North Valley, climate: temperate), CPL (Coastal Plains, climate: temperate), HGL (Highlands, climate: cold). Only HGL is cold. The file header notes 'extra kit types offered in a region are added here as their own settings', so a winter_kit setting belongs per-region in this file.", "file": "config/regions.yaml"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "config/settings.py provides load_regions() -> dict (returns the 'regions' mapping from regions.yaml), region(code: str) -> dict (raises KeyError for unknown region codes), and region_codes() -> list[str]. Region settings like winter_kit should be read via these, not by climate.", "file": "config/settings.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "WINTER-KIT is already a valid SKU: settings.SKUS = (\"FOOD-KIT\", \"HYGIENE-KIT\", \"TARP\", \"WINTER-KIT\"). reserve_stock validates sku against SKUS and raises ValueError for unknown SKUs, so WINTER-KIT reservations will work without changes.", "file": "config/settings.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "The existing reservation function is reserve_stock(warehouse_id: str, sku: str, qty: int, hold_hours: int, *, household_id: str | None = None, now=None) -> Reservation in inventory/stock.py (lines 41-66). It raises ValueError if qty <= 0 or hold_hours <= 0, so a wrapper reserving 0 must return None before calling it. If stock is insufficient it does NOT raise: it returns a Reservation with status 'pending' and empty lots. It returns a Reservation with fields id (RSV- prefixed), warehouse_id, sku, qty, lots, status, created, expires_at, household_id, and persists it to the ledger.", "file": "inventory/stock.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "allocation/rations.py line 26 already has food_kits(household: Household, today=None) -> int — the same signature shape requested for winter_kits. Its body could not be read (file service timeouts), so the exact household-size rules used for food kits (e.g. rounding/minimums) still need to be confirmed from that function before implementing winter_kits.", "file": "allocation/rations.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "tests/test_inventory.py shows usage patterns: reserve_stock(\"WH-NVL-03\", \"FOOD-KIT\", 3, 24, household_id=\"HH-10421\") and reserve_stock(\"WH-HGL-07\", \"WINTER-KIT\", 10_000, 24) (the latter presumably exercising the pending/insufficient-stock path). Warehouse IDs follow the pattern WH-<REGION>-NN, e.g. WH-HGL-07 for Highlands.", "file": "tests/test_inventory.py"}]}}

I couldn't read food_kits body or household-size rules. I should report what I know, including that food_kits exists at allocation/rations.py:26 with signature food_kits(household: Household, today=None) -> int. Also note reserve_stock raises ValueError on qty<=0, so wrapper must check qty==0 before calling. Also test shows reserve_stock("WH-HGL-07", "WINTER-KIT", 10_000, 24) — pending status when insufficient.
